correctness.rationale: The proof establishes the toric tangency condition Ax=0 with full-support kernel; irreducibility of rank<=r hollow symmetric loci for r>=3 via Gram images of irreducible isotropic quadrics; the determinant reduced and irreducible; the complete reduced Jacobian support via adjugate; codimensions through the orthogonal Gram fibers; incomparability of n+1 components; generic local quadratic cones via exact Schur complements and independent normal restrictions; and normality by Serre R1+S2. Explicit integer rank-(n-2) witnesses in sizes 5 and 6 have verified normal restriction rank three; adding invertible hyperbolic blocks retains it for every larger n. Computations are supporting finite certificates and no exhaustive-infinite inference is made.

originality.rationale: Published toric-duality and hollow rank-three descriptions do not establish the full reduced Jacobian component stratification or both generic transverse types of the n-by-n hollow determinant for all n>=5. The directly matching published n=4 quartic has a different eleven-component decomposition and cannot imply the asserted irreducible rank-(n-2) stratum in n>=5. Extensive semantic and literature searches identified no stronger covering theorem. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not a proof of global bibliographic uniqueness; see the residual full-text access risk.
residual_risks: The full text of Oldekop (2026, arXiv:2606.16482) could not be inspected; hidden overlap with the hollow discriminant cannot be completely excluded.
A general hollow determinantal singularity classification could be published under alternative matrix or A-discriminant terminology not recovered by the searches.
Only the most relevant original sections of Al Ahmadieh--Vinzant were inspected; no assertion about unrelated appendices is based on inaccessible material.

value.rationale: Projective dual singularities of the second hypersimplex are a natural and motivated geometry problem. The exact n+1 irreducible-component count, the codimension gap and non-equidimensional singular locus, and two generic transverse ordinary quadratic local models sharpen the meaning of the discriminant beyond its determinant equation and reveal a structural transition from the known n=4 eleven-component quartic. It is an infinite family structural classification, not a routine single numerical check.
